gml:Dictionary.gml:description: Codes for the cause of a delay, used for the value of the delayType property of diggs:DelayEvent. A DelayEvent records a non-productive or waiting interval together with its duration; delayType is what makes a set of them analysable, by separating avoidable downtime (breakdown, standby, materials) from ground-driven and procedurally required waiting. The three axes named in the delayType schema documentation - mechanical, operational and soil-response - are all represented. Applies wherever a DelayEvent appears: at activity level on any diggs:AbstractConstructionActivity, and on the pre-existing per-step hosts diggs:DriveSet and diggs:VaneTestMeasurementData. Built at W4 - see docs/build/W4/NOTES.md.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Delay Type Codelist Definitions

diggs:Definition.gml:description: An unplanned mechanical, hydraulic, or electrical failure of the rig, pump, or other plant that stopped production until repaired. The 'mechanical' axis named in the delayType schema documentation.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Equipment breakdown

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A planned servicing, calibration, or inspection of plant carried out during the activity. Distinguished from equipment_breakdown because it is anticipated and does not indicate equipment unreliability.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Scheduled maintenance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Relocation of the rig between element positions, including tracking, setting up, and re-levelling. Non-productive but unavoidable, and its total is a direct function of the installation sequence, so it is the delay type most useful for comparing one sequence against another.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Rig move

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Crew and plant present and available but not working - awaiting instruction, awaiting access released by another trade, or awaiting a decision. The 'operational' axis named in the delayType schema documentation.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Standby

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Awaiting delivery or availability of grout, concrete, reinforcement, or other consumables. Separated from standby because the cause is supply rather than site coordination.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Materials delay

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Suspension of work because of weather - wind limits on lifting, rainfall making the working platform untrafficable, temperature limits on grout or concrete placement.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Weather

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A delay caused by the ground's own response: an obstruction requiring removal, bore collapse or squeezing requiring re-drilling, unexpected refusal, or loss of grout to the formation. The 'soil-response' axis named in the delayType schema documentation. Where the outcome was that the element could not be completed as designed, terminationOutcome on the construction activity records that separately - this code records only the lost time.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Ground conditions

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Buried or overhead services encountered, requiring proving, diversion, or a change of position before work could resume.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Utility conflict

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Work suspended at a hold or witness point pending inspection, test results, or sign-off. The status property of the affected object carries the review state itself; this code records the production time the hold consumed.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Quality hold

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Work suspended for a safety reason - an incident, a near miss, an exclusion zone, or a site-wide stand-down.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Safety stand-down

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A waiting period required by the procedure itself rather than lost time - for example the interval between the end of penetration and the beginning of rotation in a vane test, or a required delay before a drive increment starts. Distinguished from every other code in this list because the time is specified, not lost, and excluding it is normally correct when computing non-productive time.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Procedural wait

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The working position could not be reached or occupied - haul road blocked, platform not yet constructed or handed over, or the area still occupied by preceding works.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Site access
